authorization.quote: necessary adapted and bridging dialogue is ALLOWED by default, no per-episode line cap; compression, reordering, paraphrase, and turning inner monologue into filmable action/dialogue are writer-owned; changes to a major relationship, motive, key fact or plot outcome must be listed separately as MAJOR_CHANGE
authorization.supersedes: ADAPTATION_POLICY_DRAFT.md v0 (2026-11-01), whose adapted_new=REQUIRES_LINE_OWNER default this replaces

scope.legacy_episodes: E01-E13 keep whatever they were produced under; this policy never re-judges a sealed episode

verbatim.check: the quote must occur in the cited source chapter (whitespace-insensitive fallback is reported, never silent)

condensed.check: the reason must state what was compressed and that no causal step was dropped

reorganized.check: the reason must state the causal order that is preserved

adapted_new.check: source_ref names the source beat the new line/action bridges from; trace says what it bridges between. No per-episode cap on lines.

omitted.check: a beat any later episode's source_ref depends on may not be omitted; it must be deferred

deferred.check: the episode that will carry it must be named, and it must agree with the arc ledger's hook row when one exists

major_change.description: Not a category: a flag any beat can carry. A beat flagged major_change describes a change to a major relationship, a character motive, a key established fact, or a plot outcome.
not_major: bridging dialogue that carries an existing causal link
paraphrase and compression of an existing beat
turning narration or inner monologue into a filmable action
reordering or merging scenes that keep the same causal chain
naming something the audience already saw

forbidden: using a name the audience has not been given to manufacture tension
hiding from the audience a fact the viewpoint character already knows
changing who lives or dies, or a character's established major fate, without a MAJOR_CHANGE escalation
no_quotas: no fixed number of new lines, scenes or characters per episode
no fixed number of fights, reversals or twists
